title: Private-deploy Observability Patterns — Airgapped & VPC Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for telemetry patterns we should ship for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped). It is intended for eng-observability + platform teams onboarding customers who cannot export full telemetry to our hosted systems. The doc focuses on: 1) a minimal metric set, 2) tracing strategy under egress constraints, 3) dashboard recipes that can be run locally or exported safely, and 4) a lightweight rollout/onboarding checklist.

Context & constraints (notes to self):
- Many customers in regulated industries will request zero egress of PII or PHI. Traces can leak prompt data; metrics must be privacy-first.
- On-prem infra often has limited long-term storage and different retention SLAs. Cloud-style high-cardinality traces are expensive locally.
- Operators may have only Prometheus + Grafana, or an OTel collector with local sinks. We must provide portable recipes.
- Encrypted telemetry bundles (airgap bundle) are acceptable for periodic upload after redaction, but require clear decision rules.
- Slack threads: #private-deploys, #obs-ops. See linked artifacts for draft PRs and tickets.

Design goals (prioritized):
- Safety-first: default telemetry should avoid raw request/response bodies.
- Small footprint: low-cardinality metrics, limited high-cardinality labels reserved for optional debug mode.
- Actionable: dashboards should surface SLOs, cache warmth, memory pressure, and KV cache eviction signals quickly.
- Portable: dashboard JSON + queries that work in Grafana/Prometheus or in our on-prem console.

Minimal metric set (recommended) — each metric must have a precise definition and a retention recommendation:
1) inference_requests_total (counter) — total number of inference requests accepted by gateway. Tags: tenant_id (hashed), model, route. Retain: 90d aggregated, 7d raw. Rationale: billing-surrogate and throughput.
2) inference_success_total (counter) — completion without server error (2xx). Tags: model. Retain: 90d.
3) inference_errors_total (counter) — 4xx/5xx breakdown in label 'error_class' (client|server|timeout|quota). Retain: 365d aggregated.
4) ttfb_seconds_histogram (histogram) — time to first token at service ingress (bucketed). Important for latency SLOs. Retain: 30d.
5) tokens_generated_total (counter) — total output tokens emitted by runtime. Per-model. Retain: 90d.
6) kv_cache_warmth_ratio (gauge) — fraction of requests with warm prefix/KV hit. 0-1. Retain: 30d.
7) model_memory_bytes (gauge) — resident memory for model runner. Per-server. Retain: 7d.
8) gpu_utilization_percent (gauge) — device-level utilization, 0-100. Retain: 7d.
9) queue_depth (gauge) — length of pending inference queue. 1m sampling. Retain: 30d.
10) ephemeral_trace_sample_rate (gauge) — configured sample rate; useful to debug tracing behavior.

Metric definition notes (decision rules):
- Avoid sending prompt_text or user identifiers. If tenant_id is required, it must be a one-way hash with salted key stored locally. Document the hashing scheme in onboarding.
- Keep label cardinality low. Do not use full prompt fingerprints or freeform strings as labels. Use model-version, route, and coarse tenant bucket only.
- For high-cardinality investigations, enable 'debug-mode' toggle documented below; must be authorized by customer security team and time-limited.

Tracing approach (airgapped-friendly):
- Default: no spans that include user content fields. Spans should carry only control-plane metadata (span id, parent id, model, operation, status, duration_buckets).
- Collector: Ship an OTel collector config template that writes to local file(s) and to Prometheus-style metrics where possible. Provide a redaction pipeline that strips attributes matching key patterns (prompt, input, output, user_email).
- Sampling: Use adaptive sampling. Default sample rate = 0.001 (0.1%). Provide a 'session-based' sampling tweak: sample more often when errors spike (auto ramp-up) and during rollouts.
- Trace bundling: For airgapped customers who allow periodic upload, provide an 'encrypted bundle' format (signed tar.gz) that contains only redacted traces and metrics snapshots. Uploads must be initiated by customer's admin.
- Span design: Keep spans coarse for affordability: ingress -> routing -> model_infer (single span with internal token-phase annotations) -> egress. Avoid token-level spans in default mode.

Dashboard recipes (compact, local-first):
- Dashboard A: "Service Health + SLO"
  - Panels: ttfb P50/P90/P99, inference_success_rate (inference_success_total / inference_requests_total), error_rate_timeline, queue_depth heatmap.
  - Alerting rules: ttfb P99 > 1.5x target for 10m; error_rate > 0.5% sustained 5m.
- Dashboard B: "Capacity & Cost"
  - Panels: gpu_utilization (per-host), model_memory_bytes, tokens_generated_total rate, kv_cache_warmth_ratio trend.
  - Note: use derived rate panels to show tokens-per-second normalized to GPU utilization.
- Dashboard C: "Debug Mode" (hidden by default)
  - Panels: high-cardinality error breakdown, sampled traces list (link to local trace viewer), debug-mode toggle state.
  - Access: RBAC-protected; show instructions on how to enable and expire debug mode.

Onboarding checklist (for solutions_eng + customer):
- Preflight: confirm allowed telemetry egress and required redaction policies. Documented in SOW.
- Install: provide OTel collector + prom stack recipe. Validate versions.
- Apply: default obs config (metrics only, low-cardinality labels). Enable tracing disabled by default.
- Smoke tests: run synthetic probe (3x p50/p99 synthetics) under test tenant. Verify KV warmth metric moves.
- Permissions: set RBAC for debug dashboards and enable expiry for debug-mode.
- Handover: deliver dashboard JSON and runbook PDF. Provide Confluence page for incident steps.

Runbook snippets (for oncall):
- If ttfb P99 increases > 2x: check queue_depth -> check gpu_utilization -> check model_memory_bytes -> test sample trace (if debug-mode on).
- If kv_cache_warmth_ratio drops > 30%: look at recent deploys (routing changes), check model versions, warm-up synthetic probe.
- If inference_errors_total spikes: group by error_class, check backend dependencies (model loader timeouts, disk IO).

Privacy & compliance guardrails (must include in customer SOW):
- Default telemetry collection excludes any attribute named input*, prompt*, output*, user_*; any telemetry that could reasonably contain PII must be opt-in and timeboxed.
- Debug-mode requires signed approval from customer security owner; automatic revocation after N hours (configurable).
- Provide a documented redaction test: run sample traces through redaction pipeline and store hash of redacted output for audit.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we provide a small hosted "redaction-as-a-service" appliance customers can run locally to validate bundles before upload? Pros: easier audit. Cons: extra surface area.
- How do we record provenance of hashed tenant_id (salt rotation)? Need ops guidance.
- Investigate compact trace format for offline analysis (binary vs JSONL). Proposed: JSONL with compressed attributes.

Appendix: useful quick commands and links
- Prometheus scrape example: minimal scrape config snippet (see linked_confluence page).
- Grafana dashboard export: attach dashboard JSON in Confluence under /obs/private-dashboards.
- Quick debug command: curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_cache_warmth_ratio

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this as a living doc during Q2 pilot with 3 customers. Expect many edits from solutions eng.
- Coordinate with security and legal for SOW language.
- Next step: draft OTel collector templates and a redaction CI job (PR referenced above).

-- Maya
